# PUT /api/v1/notifications

Mark notification threads as read, unread, or pinned for the current user

**Module:** [routers](../modules/routers.md) · **Auth:** bearer (notification scope, write) · **ID:** `ep-020`

## Request

| Param | Location | Type | Required |
|-------|----------|------|----------|
| last_read_at | query | string (RFC3339) | False |
| all | query | string | False |
| status-types | query | []string | False |
| to-status | query | string | False |

**Headers:** `Authorization`

## Response

**205** — []NotificationThread

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | int64 | Notification thread ID |
| `repository` | Repository | Associated repository |
| `subject` | NotificationSubject | Notification subject details |
| `unread` | bool | Whether notification is unread |
| `pinned` | bool | Whether notification is pinned |
| `updated_at` | time.Time | Last update timestamp |
| `url` | string | API URL for this thread |

- **400** — Invalid last_read_at timestamp format
- **401** — No valid token provided
- **403** — Token lacks notification write scope

## Business Rules

| Rule | Category | Condition |
|------|----------|-----------|
| Notification status-types defaults to [unread] when not specified for read/mark endpoints | validation | !ctx.FormBool("all") && len(statuses) == 0 |
| When 'all' flag is true, no status filter is applied (all statuses are included) | business_logic | ctx.FormBool("all") == true |
| Default target status for marking notifications is 'read' when to-status is not specified or invalid | business_logic | targetStatus == 0 (invalid or empty to-status) |
| Notification endpoints require token with notification scope category | authorization | Token is API token with scope |
| Notification thread access is restricted to the owning user or admin | authorization | n.UserID != ctx.Doer.ID && !ctx.Doer.IsAdmin |
| SetNotificationStatus verifies the notification belongs to the requesting user before updating | business_logic | notification.UserID != user.ID |
| Repository info is omitted from notification response if user's access has been revoked | business_logic | !perm.HasAnyUnitAccessOrPublicAccess() |

## ⚠️ Performance Issues

| Severity | Type | Description | Recommendation |
|----------|------|-------------|----------------|
| high | n_plus_1_queries | SetNotificationStatus is called in a loop: each iteration does SELECT by ID + UPDATE. Then LoadAttributes does 4 individual queries per notification. | Use a single bulk UPDATE query with WHERE id IN (...) and batch load attributes |
| high | unbounded_queries | The initial db.Find has no pagination (ListOptions is zero-value). All matching notifications are loaded into memory. | Add a reasonable limit or use pagination. Consider processing in batches. |

### Optimization Recommendations

- **[P0] query_optimization**: Replace per-notification SetNotificationStatus loop with bulk UPDATE — *Impact: Reduce N*2 queries to 1 bulk UPDATE + 1 bulk SELECT*
- **[P1] pagination**: Add a limit to the unbounded find query or process in batches — *Impact: Prevent memory exhaustion and timeout for users with many notifications*

## 🛡️ Resiliency

**Risk Level:** medium

| Pattern | Status | Severity | Detail |
|---------|--------|----------|--------|
| non_atomic | ❌ missing | medium | Updates notifications one-by-one in a loop without a transaction. If the loop fails midway, some notifications are marked read while others remain unread. |
| idempotency | ✅ configured | low | Setting notification status is idempotent - retrying sets the same status again |
